title: The CRW four-month outlook rules alone give its 3.7-times Alert over-forecast: a perfect-SST emulation at 3,595 reef cells (2019-2025) matches the measured error
abstract: Question: what causes the Alert over-forecast of the NOAA Coral Reef Watch (CRW) Four-Month Coral Bleaching Outlook? The earlier SCI study a1c89b0a measured Alert 1+ probabilities 3-4 times too high at weeks 9-20 (2019-2026) and suggested a warm model SST offset. Approach: the outlook adds every predicted HotSpot above a threshold that falls from 1 deg C at lead day 0 to 0 deg C at day 70; the satellite product adds only HotSpots of at least 1 deg C. We applied the published outlook rules to observed SST (NOAA OISST v2.1) as a perfect forecast at 3,595 reef cells for 329 weekly issues (2019-04 to 2025-08), and compared with the satellite rules on the same SST. We measured the sub-monthly SST damping of 36 CFSv2 forecasts. Six predictions were pre-registered; all passed. Result: with a perfect forecast the rules give Alert 1+ observed/expected 1.23 at week 1 and 0.27 (95% interval 0.23-0.31) at weeks 9-20; the measured outlook value is 0.25. The rule explains 0.94 (0.85-1.05) of the measured log error, and the pattern by issue year (Spearman 0.89), region (0.94) and reef cell (0.69). CFSv2 sub-monthly variability is 0.76-0.80 of OISST and does not change with lead; even with no sub-monthly variability the rules give 0.27, so the ramp corrects for damping about 5 times too strongly. A long-lead threshold near 0.8-0.9 deg C would be neutral. In a 1985-2025 emulation the rule-only false-Alert excess rose from 1.6% to 14.6% of reef cell-weeks as heat just above the climatological maximum increased. Limitations: the emulation has no model bias or ensemble spread; short-lead (weeks 1-4) errors are not explained; truth is OISST, not the CRW 5km product.

display.caption: Observed/expected (log scale) by lead week for Alert 1+, Warning+ and Watch+. Blue: measured CRW outlook error (a1c89b0a, bin mid and bin range). Orange: perfect SST forecast run through the published outlook rules. Green and violet: forecast SST with reduced or no sub-monthly variability. Grey dashed: perfect SST with the satellite 1 deg C threshold at all leads. Issues 2019-04 to 2025-08, 3,595 reef cells.

CFSv2 sub-monthly SST variability at reef cells as a fraction of OISST (36 operational runs, 95% run-bootstrap intervals) is constant near 0.78, while the published HotSpot threshold falls from 1 to 0 deg C by day 70.

Left: Alert 1+ frequency at weeks 9-20 by issue year 1985-2025: satellite-rule truth, perfect SST with the published rule, and perfect SST with a 1 deg C threshold. Right: annual HotSpot sums per reef pixel below and above 1 deg C.

citations.reason: Measured outlook error tables and reef cells. We support its finding that Alert probabilities are too high at long leads and challenge its suggested cause (a warm model SST offset): the published threshold rule alone gives the measured excess.
Outlook algorithm (Table 1, Figure 1): lead-time dependent HotSpot and DHW thresholds that we emulate and test.
